blockers.description: CLI and dashboard report DIFFERENT scores for the SAME single clean scan: report 15/100 with 5 CRITICAL, dashboard 19/100 with 7 CRITICAL. ROOT CAUSE FOUND: the SAML IdP publishes ONE certificate (serial 109f9643...) under two `use` values (signing + encryption), so crypto_endpoints holds two rows and scan.py:480-498 emits one CRITICAL per ROW — one weak 1024-bit key becomes two CRITICALs, and CRITICAL count drives the score cap. The use=encryption row is also mislabelled 'Weak SAML SIGNING certificate'. Separately the CLI omits the SAML finding entirely despite scoring it. SESSION_BRACKET=5min is a THIRD, independent issue that merges scans under 5 minutes apart (34 certs, 14 CRITICAL) — it is NOT what causes the 15-vs-19 gap.

decisions.decision: A test the previous handoff listed as a stale pin was NOT stale — it caught a real model defect
decisions.rationale: test_identity_surface::test_weak_kerberos_lowers_score exposed a live P1 violation: the compression guard read `total_score > _ceiling`, applying compression only ABOVE the ceiling. A piecewise linear map is not order-preserving, so computed 84 emitted 84 while computed 85 emitted 71, and nothing in [85,100] ever emitted more than 84. Every well-run estate scored below a mediocre one. The ladder could not see it — all five rungs already computed above their own ceilings — which is why the fix moves the ladder by zero points.

decisions.decision: Register P2b's xfail rather than delete the marker
decisions.rationale: Every other entry in tests/skip_registry.py records an environment gap; P2b is a known OPEN DEFECT kept numeric so it cannot decay into prose. First xfail the ledger has carried, hence the new known_open_defect category. The gate checks both directions, so when P2b is fixed and the marker deleted, the entry becomes an orphan and fails — it cannot outlive the defect.

decisions.decision: Do NOT promote P2b's [20] parameter despite it XPASSing
decisions.rationale: It passed by a rounding coincidence — round(25*71/100) and round(25*74/100) both land on 18 under half-to-even — while the computed score still rose. Promoting it would encode a rounding artifact as a green gate. The property now also asserts the pre-ceiling value via _computed_score() and fails honestly at all three parameters.

decisions.decision: Fix /print structurally (don't mount the chrome) rather than with CSS
decisions.rationale: Hiding the sidebar from PrintPage's own <style> block would couple the client deliverable to sidebar class names and Tailwind margin utilities; rename either and the sidebar silently reappears in client PDFs, a regression whose only witness is the client. The early return stays INSIDE status === 'authenticated' — the PDF renderer reaches /print only via the documented auth-disabled passthrough, so hoisting it above the gate would turn an authenticated view anonymous.

context_notes: SCORING v3 IS THE STORY. The multihost estate scored 91/100 under v2 and scores 15/100 POOR under v3 on IDENTICAL evidence — a 76-point move that fixes the P1 denominator blindness the oracle documented. The old demo guidance ('lead with findings, the score is misleading') is now REVERSED and the oracle says so. THREE THINGS A RESUMING AGENT SHOULD NOT MISREAD. (1) A stale prober image silently reproduces 91/100 with no warning and exit 0 — always verify SCORING_VERSION inside the container before quoting a score, and use `-p chaoslab` or the rebuild tags the wrong image and does nothing. (2) The per-host oracle rows now carry measured finding TITLES, not just counts, because the previous rows had the COUNT right and the MEANING wrong for two hosts (the S3 host's 2 HIGHs are plaintext-HTTP, not the unencrypted bucket; the Redis host's MEDIUM is a blocked handshake, not a cleartext-broker finding). (3) `pytest -k "scor"` still misses a third of the scoring surface — select with $(grep -rln "quirk.intelligence.scoring" tests/); that selection ran green at 439 passed / 3 xfailed after these edits.
